page: OVHcloud i1-45 is a storage-optimized server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Haswell architecture running at 2.2 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 45.0 GB of RAM, providing 5.62 GB per core. Storage is a key component of this instance, bundling 1950 GB of local storage split between 1900 GB of NVMe and 50 GB of SSD. Network connectivity is supported by a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 8940.1 and a Passmark CPU score of 9710.85. Memory bandwidth remains consistently average, reaching 64.85 GB/sec for large block reads and 34.08 GB/sec for large block writes. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform in the average tier, with Redis achieving 10.09 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the i1-45 instance lies in its older Intel Haswell CPU architecture, which lacks modern instruction sets like AVX-512 but retains standard AVX and AES cryptography support. This results in slower single-threaded execution, such as poor gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds. Qualitatively, the instance offers high resource density for storage-heavy workloads, providing a cost-effective option for scenarios requiring substantial local NVMe capacity without needing top-tier compute performance. It is best suited for database hosting, static web serving, and distributed storage nodes where local read/write speeds are prioritized over raw single-core processing power.
